What is the next step after the book?

Thank you for reading The Naturalization Interview & Immigration Medical Exam Guide. If you need the immigration medical exam, the quickest next step is the callback button above: a civil surgeon near you calls you back. It is one short request, free to you, and we never ask for details of your case. Only a civil surgeon designated by USCIS can complete Form I-693.

Prefer to search yourself? The official USCIS civil surgeon finder lists every designated civil surgeon by ZIP code, and the free checklists below help you compare two or three before you book.

If you are preparing for the naturalization interview instead, start with which civics test applies to you; it depends only on the date you filed Form N-400.

How does the free callback work?

Yes, if you want it. You can ask for a callback from a civil surgeon in your area through this site. It is free to you, it asks only for an email address and an optional ZIP code, and it never asks for details of your case. We do not rank providers, and a provider may pay a listing or referral fee; that never changes the guides. Always confirm a provider in the official USCIS finder before you book.

Questions readers ask

Do I need the medical exam for naturalization?

Usually not. Form I-693, the immigration medical exam, is part of applying for a green card (adjustment of status), not of the N-400 naturalization interview. A naturalization applicant may see a doctor only for a disability exception, which uses a different form, N-648.

Who can do the immigration medical exam?

Only a civil surgeon that USCIS has designated. Any other doctor's exam is not accepted for Form I-693. The official USCIS finder lists designated civil surgeons by ZIP code.

Is this site part of USCIS?

No. USCIS Exam Guides is an independent educational site. It is not affiliated with USCIS, does not file anything for you and gives no legal or medical advice. For your case, rely on USCIS and a qualified immigration attorney or accredited representative.
